newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan holds military drills, says non-political.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan holds military drills, says non-political.

text.p: Taiwan's armed forces practised making -- and preventing -- amphibious landings on Tuesday in what a military spokesman called a routine annual drill with "no political implications".
The manoeuvres involved 80 ships and more than 10,000 soldiers at a navy base in southern Pingtung county, the state-funded Central News Agency reported.
Amphibious skills are central to the Nationalist-ruled island's defences against rival China, which has pledged to retake the island by force if it declares independence.
China's communist government has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since a civil war split them in 1949.
Military spokesman Kung Fan-ting, quoted by the agency, described the exercises as routine, normal and apolitical.
"They have no political implications whatsoever," Kung said. "There is no need to imply any political motivation."

China held war games and missile tests near Taiwan around the island's first direct presidential election in March in what Beijing acknowledged was a bid to warn Taiwanese voters not to drop a state pledge to reunify with the mainland.

Taiwan postponed a planned April military exercise to avoid exacerbating tension. The siuation eased after the March 23 election, but the sides remain deeply suspicious of each other and Beijing has blocked resumption of semi-official talks which it froze in mid-1995.
